title: Micro-interaction research: console session notes (keyboard-first & cost signals)
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick, focused usability sessions to validate micro-interactions in the Console that affect inference cost signals and keyboard-first workflows.
- Hypotheses: inline cost/latency hints reduce surprise; keyboard shortcuts and clear affordances speed up routine config changes; small animation feedback improves trust for toggles that change routing (eg: cost -> lower latency vs cheaper).

Session logistics:
- Date: 2024-09-18 (pilot) + 2024-09-24 (n=6 customers)
- Participants: 6 (3 ML engineers, 2 backend/platform engineers, 1 product manager)
- Format: remote moderated (30-40m), prototype in Figma + interactive HTML microflows for the cost toggle and model-pin modal.
- Key tasks:
  1) Set up a route to prefer lower-latency model while keeping a cost budget.
  2) Change batching strategy and confirm expected cost delta.
  3) Pin a model version for canary rollout and preview fallback behavior.

Top findings (summary):
- Clear win: small in-line cost chips next to model names (e.g., "$0.004/1k tokens") were used by all participants within the first 30s; they reported being more comfortable making routing changes when cost was visible.
- Keyboard-first flow: Cmd/Ctrl+K to open quick action palette was discovered by 4/6 users when hinted; those who used it completed tasks ~25% faster. Suggestion: surface a short hint the first time user lands on Routes page.
- Toggle feedback: participants expected immediate, non-blocking confirmation when toggling autoscale or fallback policies. A subtle micro-animation (0.12s) and toast with short sentence ("Fallback enabled — requests will route to model-B if model-A saturates") increased perceived safety.
- Danger of overload: too many inline chips (cost, latency, throughput, quantization) felt noisy. Participants recommended progressive disclosure: show cost + latency by default, other metrics behind expand chevron.
- Mental model mismatch: some platform engineers equated "pin model" with immutable routing; they expected a separate UI to manage rollbacks. Need clearer copy and an explicit "rollback" timeline.

Representative quotes:
- "If I can see the cost right where I change a route, I don't have to go hunting through billing pages." — ML eng
- "Short keyboard hints are great, but don't hide them completely. I want to learn the shortcut without reading docs." — Platform eng
- "That tiny animation made me feel like something actually changed. I knew to check the logs after toggling." — Product manager

Wireframe/writeup notes (things to iterate in Figma):
- Route list row: left: model avatar + name; center: short description; right: primary CTA group with "pin" (icon), cost chip, latency chip, kebab for advanced.
- Cost chip design: two states: normal (value + tooltip) and caution (if budget would be exceeded by change). Tooltip contains sample calc: "Est. +$0.12 / hr at 50 TPS (95th pct sequence)."
- Quick action palette: searchable list, keyboard-first; entries: Create route, Edit route, Pin model, Open rollout. Add ephemeral hint "Press / to search routes" visible first time.
- Toggle animation: 0.12s fade + 0.06s slide to indicate state. Keep motion minimal for SLO impressions.
- Model pin modal: show pin effect (preview traffic %), rollback link, and a small timeline control (slider) for phased rollout. Provide clear copy: "Pin model X — only routes that explicitly prefer pinned models will hit this version."

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets / priorities):
- JIRA-UX-987: Implement cost + latency chips on route rows (priority: P0 for hosted customers).
- JIRA-ENG-4321: Quick action palette keyboard deltas + analytics (P1).
- JIRA-UX-998: Toggle micro-animation + toast templates (P2).
- JIRA-PROD-1012: Rollout timeline UI (phased slider) + rollback CTA (P1).
- Notes: split JIRA-ENG-4321 into frontend + telemetry tasks. Frontend should default to accessible focus states for keyboard nav.

Accessibility & edge cases:
- Ensure chips have visible focus rings and aria-labels for screen readers (cost chip aria: "estimated cost per 1k tokens: $0.004").
- Test with larger token-cost numbers and localized currency formatting.
- Offline/slow network: toggles should optimistically update but show pending spinner; if update fails, show inline error with rollback affordance.

Unresolved questions / research follow-ups:
- How much cost precision is useful? Participants varied between wanting a rounded number vs detailed breakdown by token type. Recommendation: default to rounded, expandable detail view.
- Should cost estimates be based on 95th percentile sequence lengths by default or user-set sample? Add quick setting in profile.
- Which CTA language reduces rollback anxiety: "Pin model" vs "Promote model"? Run A/B in next usability batch.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Aisha: update Figma wireframes with chips + quick palette hint (due 2024-10-07).
- Tom: spike keyboard palette implementation options & accessibility implications; record a short demo (due 2024-10-04).
- Leah: scope telemetry for chip impressions + palette usage (linked to JIRA-ENG-4321) (due 2024-10-09).
- Carlos: draft copy options for pin/promotion wording, prepare 2 variants for A/B test (due 2024-10-06).

Notes to self / rough brainstorm (raw):
- Consider putting a small "cost impact preview" when you hover the model name that simulates 1,000 tokens at current default sequence length (fast mental math).
- Could we attach a "safe-mode" toggle that momentarily slows autoscaling to prefer cheaper paths for non-critical traffic? (ops concern)
- Link to billing: add a fast path to open cost insights filtered to the selected route.

- Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234-console-micro-interactions
- Prototype HTML (interactive toggles): https://internal-prototypes.redwood.ai/micro-toggle-2024-09
- Raw session recordings (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/recordings/console-micro-20240918.zip

Next steps: finalize wireframes -> create UX tickets -> split frontend spike -> include SRE review for optimistic toggles.

Status: moving to in_review once Figma updates land. This doc is a working record; expect iterations.

-- Aisha (notes)
